answer:
Mix the one-hot target with a uniform distribution over all classes: (1−eps)·one_hot + eps/C. This gives (1−eps) times ordinary NLL plus eps times the negative mean log probability. The all-class convention matches PyTorch; distributing smoothing only over incorrect classes is a different formula. Compute log_softmax once for stability.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** With $C$ classes, smoothed labels are $q_c=(1-\epsilon)\mathbf1[c=y]+\epsilon/C$. Thus $L=(1-\epsilon)(-\log p_y)-\epsilon C^{-1}\sum_c\log p_c$. The target still sums to one, so the logit gradient is $p-q$. Smoothing changes the optimization target and can affect confidence/calibration as well as accuracy. [3](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://gombru.github.io/2018/05/23/cross_entropy_loss/) and [2](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss.html).
